questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank:
There are good points to each side and we need more ________ people that are willing to look at them from all angles.
questions.explanation: 'Unbiased' means fair and impartial, which fits people who are willing to look at an issue from all angles. 'Opinionated' means the opposite.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bold word:
This medicine can make you feel **lethargic** and dizzy.
questions.explanation: 'Lethargic' means sluggish, lacking energy, i.e. inactive. 'Kinetic' and 'energetic' are its opposites.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom:
"Through thick and thin"

options.A: To work hard to the point of exhaustion
options.C: Only in times of great difficulty

questions.explanation: 'Through thick and thin' means under all circumstances, in good times as well as bad times.

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
Passage: Strong mental health is not just the (1)______ of mental health problems. (2)______ mentally or emotionally healthy is (3)______ more than being free of depression, anxiety or other psychological issues. (4)______ than the absence of mental illness, mental health (5)______ to the presence of positive characteristics and positive outlook towards life.
questions.explanation: The passage says mental health is not just the 'absence' of mental health problems; the last sentence repeats the idea with 'absence of mental illness'.

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
Passage: Strong mental health is not just the (1)______ of mental health problems. (2)______ mentally or emotionally healthy is (3)______ more than being free of depression, anxiety or other psychological issues. (4)______ than the absence of mental illness, mental health (5)______ to the presence of positive characteristics and positive outlook towards life.
questions.explanation: A gerund is needed as the subject of the sentence: 'Being mentally or emotionally healthy is ...'.

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
Passage: Strong mental health is not just the (1)______ of mental health problems. (2)______ mentally or emotionally healthy is (3)______ more than being free of depression, anxiety or other psychological issues. (4)______ than the absence of mental illness, mental health (5)______ to the presence of positive characteristics and positive outlook towards life.
questions.explanation: With a comparative ('more than'), the intensifier is 'much': 'is much more than being free of depression'.

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
Passage: Strong mental health is not just the (1)______ of mental health problems. (2)______ mentally or emotionally healthy is (3)______ more than being free of depression, anxiety or other psychological issues. (4)______ than the absence of mental illness, mental health (5)______ to the presence of positive characteristics and positive outlook towards life.
questions.explanation: 'Rather than' expresses preference or contrast: 'Rather than the absence of mental illness, mental health refers to ...'.

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
Passage: Strong mental health is not just the (1)______ of mental health problems. (2)______ mentally or emotionally healthy is (3)______ more than being free of depression, anxiety or other psychological issues. (4)______ than the absence of mental illness, mental health (5)______ to the presence of positive characteristics and positive outlook towards life.
questions.explanation: The verb that takes 'to' and means 'denotes' here is 'refers': 'mental health refers to the presence of positive characteristics'.

questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी पश्चिमी हिंदी की बोली है?
questions.explanation: Western Hindi includes Khadi Boli, Brajbhasha, Haryanvi, Bundeli and Kannauji. Garhwali is Pahari, Malvi is Rajasthani and Awadhi is Eastern Hindi.

questions.question: हिंदी में ( ; ) विराम चिह्न का नाम क्या है?
questions.explanation: ( ; ) is अर्द्धविराम (semicolon). अल्पविराम is the comma ( , ) and निर्देशक चिह्न is the dash.

questions.question: 'मूर्खता' शब्द में कौन-सा प्रत्यय प्रयुक्त हुआ है?
questions.explanation: मूर्ख + ता = मूर्खता. 'ता' is a suffix that forms abstract nouns (भाववाचक संज्ञा).

questions.question: 'हट' से अंत होने वाली भाववाचक संज्ञाएँ (जैसे घबराहट, मुस्कुराहट) किस लिंग की होती हैं?
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns ending in 'हट' and 'वट' are feminine: घबराहट, सजावट. Hindi has no neuter gender.

questions.question: हिंदी में कुल कितने सर्वनाम हैं?
questions.explanation: Hindi has 11 basic pronouns: मैं, तू, आप, यह, वह, जो, सो, कौन, क्या, कोई, कुछ. 6 is the number of types (भेद) of pronouns.

questions.question: "दिनेश रोज चार लीटर दूध पीता है।" वाक्य में 'चार लीटर' कौन-सा विशेषण है?
questions.explanation: 'चार लीटर' indicates a measured quantity (माप-तौल) of milk, so it is a निश्चित परिमाणवाचक विशेषण, not संख्यावाचक which counts countable things.

questions.question: 'वह शाम को घर जाएगा।' वाक्य में कौन-सी वृत्ति (अर्थ) प्रयुक्त हुई है?
questions.explanation: The sentence states a definite action, so it is निश्चयार्थ. सम्भावनार्थ would be 'वह शायद जाए'.

questions.question: जो क्रिया अभी हो रही है, उसके काल को क्या कहते हैं?
questions.explanation: An action in progress at present (e.g. 'वह पढ़ रहा है') is अपूर्ण (तात्कालिक) वर्तमान काल.

questions.question: "कटोरे भर उसने खीर खाई।" वाक्य में अनुबद्ध संबंधबोधक अव्यय कौन-सा शब्द है?
questions.explanation: अनुबद्ध संबंधबोधक comes after the inflected (विकारी) form of a noun. 'भर' follows 'कटोरे' and shows the relation.

questions.question: 'जिस पर आक्रमण किया गया हो' वाक्यांश के लिए एक शब्द चुनिए:
questions.explanation: One who has been attacked is आक्रांत. आक्रामक is one who attacks.

questions.question: किस मुहावरे का अर्थ 'सावधान करना' है?
questions.explanation: 'कान खोलना' means to make someone alert. 'कान भरना' means to poison someone's ears (चुगली करना).

questions.question: कौन-सा शब्द अव्ययीभाव समास का उदाहरण नहीं है?
questions.explanation: आमरण, यथासाध्य and प्रतिदिन begin with an indeclinable (अव्यय) and are अव्ययीभाव. श्रमसाध्य (श्रम से साध्य) is करण तत्पुरुष.

questions.question: किस शब्द की वर्तनी सही है?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is मंगलाचरण (मंगल + आचरण).

questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विलोम युग्म सही है?
questions.explanation: चिरंतन (eternal) is the opposite of नश्वर (perishable). The other pairs are synonyms.

questions.question: रिक्त स्थान के लिए उपयुक्त शब्द चुनिए: "______ हो तो प्रकाश को कौन पूछे।"
questions.explanation: The sense is that light is valued only because of darkness; 'अंधकार' completes the sentence logically.

questions.question: रिक्त स्थान के लिए उपयुक्त शब्द चुनिए: मैं मंत्री की ______ से आपको धन्यवाद देता हूँ।
questions.explanation: 'की हैसियत से' means 'in the capacity of'. The speaker thanks in the capacity of a minister.

questions.question: भयानक रस का स्थायी भाव क्या है?
questions.explanation: भयानक रस - भय. विस्मय belongs to अद्भुत रस, क्रोध to रौद्र रस and जुगुप्सा to वीभत्स रस.

questions.question:
हिंदी गद्यांश को पढ़कर रिक्त स्थान (1) के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त शब्द चुनिए:
गद्यांश: अपना स्वभाव छोड़ना किसी के (1)______ में नहीं है। दुष्ट एवं स्वार्थी को पहचान कर वैसे ही चलना चाहिए जैसे कीचड़ भरे मार्ग में हम बचते हुए चलते हैं। दुष्ट व्यक्ति कुछ पल के लिए अपना (2)______ बदल सकता है परन्तु (3)______ मिलते ही वह अपनी दुष्टता पर उतारू हो जाएगा। करेला मीठा नहीं हो सकता एवं साँप विष की जगह (4)______ नहीं उगल सकता। पाँचों (5)______ बराबर नहीं होती।
questions.explanation: 'किसी के बस में नहीं' means not within anyone's control; giving up one's nature is not in anyone's control.

questions.question:
हिंदी गद्यांश को पढ़कर रिक्त स्थान (2) के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त शब्द चुनिए:
गद्यांश: अपना स्वभाव छोड़ना किसी के (1)______ में नहीं है। दुष्ट एवं स्वार्थी को पहचान कर वैसे ही चलना चाहिए जैसे कीचड़ भरे मार्ग में हम बचते हुए चलते हैं। दुष्ट व्यक्ति कुछ पल के लिए अपना (2)______ बदल सकता है परन्तु (3)______ मिलते ही वह अपनी दुष्टता पर उतारू हो जाएगा। करेला मीठा नहीं हो सकता एवं साँप विष की जगह (4)______ नहीं उगल सकता। पाँचों (5)______ बराबर नहीं होती।
questions.explanation: A wicked person may change his behaviour (व्यवहार) for a moment, but not his nature.

questions.question:
हिंदी गद्यांश को पढ़कर रिक्त स्थान (3) के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त शब्द चुनिए:
गद्यांश: अपना स्वभाव छोड़ना किसी के (1)______ में नहीं है। दुष्ट एवं स्वार्थी को पहचान कर वैसे ही चलना चाहिए जैसे कीचड़ भरे मार्ग में हम बचते हुए चलते हैं। दुष्ट व्यक्ति कुछ पल के लिए अपना (2)______ बदल सकता है परन्तु (3)______ मिलते ही वह अपनी दुष्टता पर उतारू हो जाएगा। करेला मीठा नहीं हो सकता एवं साँप विष की जगह (4)______ नहीं उगल सकता। पाँचों (5)______ बराबर नहीं होती।
questions.explanation: 'अवसर मिलते ही' means as soon as he gets an opportunity, he returns to his wickedness.

questions.question:
हिंदी गद्यांश को पढ़कर रिक्त स्थान (4) के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त शब्द चुनिए:
गद्यांश: अपना स्वभाव छोड़ना किसी के (1)______ में नहीं है। दुष्ट एवं स्वार्थी को पहचान कर वैसे ही चलना चाहिए जैसे कीचड़ भरे मार्ग में हम बचते हुए चलते हैं। दुष्ट व्यक्ति कुछ पल के लिए अपना (2)______ बदल सकता है परन्तु (3)______ मिलते ही वह अपनी दुष्टता पर उतारू हो जाएगा। करेला मीठा नहीं हो सकता एवं साँप विष की जगह (4)______ नहीं उगल सकता। पाँचों (5)______ बराबर नहीं होती।
questions.explanation: A snake cannot spit nectar (अमृत) instead of poison: the natural opposite of विष is अमृत.

questions.question:
हिंदी गद्यांश को पढ़कर रिक्त स्थान (5) के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त शब्द चुनिए:
गद्यांश: अपना स्वभाव छोड़ना किसी के (1)______ में नहीं है। दुष्ट एवं स्वार्थी को पहचान कर वैसे ही चलना चाहिए जैसे कीचड़ भरे मार्ग में हम बचते हुए चलते हैं। दुष्ट व्यक्ति कुछ पल के लिए अपना (2)______ बदल सकता है परन्तु (3)______ मिलते ही वह अपनी दुष्टता पर उतारू हो जाएगा। करेला मीठा नहीं हो सकता एवं साँप विष की जगह (4)______ नहीं उगल सकता। पाँचों (5)______ बराबर नहीं होती।
questions.explanation: The proverb 'पाँचों उँगलियाँ बराबर नहीं होतीं' means all people are not alike.

questions.question: Which was the only session of the Indian National Congress presided over by Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.explanation: Gandhi presided over only the 1924 Belgaum session. The 1929 Lahore session was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.question: Who among the following was the government lawyer (public prosecutor) in the Kakori conspiracy case?
questions.explanation: Jagat Narayan Mulla was the government counsel. Govind Ballabh Pant and Mohanlal Saxena were among the defence counsel.

questions.question: What was the message of John Ruskin's book "Unto This Last" that transformed Mahatma Gandhi?

options.A: Non-violence is the only weapon against injustice
options.B: It is the moral duty of the educated to uplift the exploited and the poor
options.C: The welfare of the individual lies in the welfare of all
options.D: Celibacy and spiritual contemplation are essential for a higher life

questions.explanation: Gandhi summarised Ruskin's teaching as: the good of the individual is contained in the good of all; all work has equal value; the life of labour is worth living. He named his paraphrase 'Sarvodaya'.

questions.question: Why did the Indian National Congress oppose the Rowlatt Act (1919)?

options.A: It aimed to extend communal representation
options.B: It aimed to increase land revenue
options.C: It aimed to ban the Indian National Congress
options.D: It aimed to restrict personal freedom

questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Act allowed detention without trial and curbed civil liberties, which is why it was called the 'Black Act'.

questions.question: In which city was the 1920 Khilafat Committee meeting held, where Gandhi was requested to lead the Non-Cooperation Movement?
questions.explanation: The Khilafat Committee met at Allahabad in June 1920 and asked Gandhi to lead non-cooperation. The Congress special session at Calcutta (Sept 1920) adopted the programme.

questions.question: Why did Mahatma Gandhi support the Khilafat Movement?

options.A: To establish a separate Muslim homeland
options.B: To gain the cooperation of Indian Muslims in the movement against the British
options.C: The Khalifa had given shelter to Indian revolutionaries
options.D: The Khalifa had supported India's freedom struggle

questions.explanation: Gandhi saw the Khilafat issue as an opportunity to build Hindu-Muslim unity in a joint national movement against British rule.

questions.question: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress on 15 August 1947?
questions.explanation: Acharya J.B. Kripalani was Congress President in 1946-47 and held the post at independence. Nehru became Prime Minister.

questions.question: Which centenary celebration was inaugurated by the Prime Minister in February 2021?
questions.explanation: The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 4 February 1922; its centenary celebrations were inaugurated on 4 February 2021.

questions.question: Where is the Okhla Bird Sanctuary located?

options.A: NCR region (Gautam Buddh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh)

questions.explanation: Okhla Bird Sanctuary lies on the Yamuna at the Delhi-Noida border in Gautam Buddh Nagar district, in the NCR.

questions.question: Where was India's first jute mill established before independence?
questions.explanation: The first jute mill was set up at Rishra near Calcutta, Bengal, in 1855. Gujarat and Maharashtra were cotton textile centres.

questions.question: What is the black soil used for cotton cultivation called?
questions.explanation: Black soil, rich in clay and moisture-retentive, is called Regur or black cotton soil and is found in the Deccan plateau.

questions.question: What material was used to build Hawa Mahal in Jaipur?
questions.explanation: Hawa Mahal (1799), built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, is made of red and pink sandstone.

questions.question: Among the following, which Indian state shares its boundary with the maximum number of other Indian states?
questions.explanation: Among the options, Assam borders the most states (7: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya, West Bengal). Overall, Uttar Pradesh borders the most states.

questions.question: Which is the world's first fully solar-powered airport?
questions.explanation: Cochin International Airport (Kerala) became the world's first fully solar-powered airport in 2015.

questions.question: Which Indian state has the largest forest area?
questions.explanation: By area, Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover (ISFR). Arunachal Pradesh ranks high but second; Mizoram leads by percentage.

questions.question: How many bio-geographical zones are there in India?
questions.explanation: India has 10 bio-geographic zones (Rodgers and Panwar): Trans-Himalaya, Himalaya, Desert, Semi-arid, Western Ghats, Deccan Plateau, Gangetic Plain, North-East, Coasts and Islands.

questions.concept: Object at focus of concave mirror
questions.question: If an object is placed in front of a concave mirror at a distance equal to its focal length, where will the image be formed?

options.C: At a point between P and F

questions.explanation: When the object is at F, reflected rays are parallel, so a highly enlarged real image forms at infinity.

questions.question: Work in physics is defined as:

options.A: A force applied on a body that does not displace it
options.B: The rate of change of momentum of a body
options.C: The product of force and the displacement in the direction of the force
options.D: The product of force and the time for which it acts

questions.explanation: W = F × s × cos θ. If there is no displacement, no work is done. Rate of change of momentum is force; force × time is impulse.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about two vectors having unequal magnitudes?

options.A: Their resultant can never be zero
options.D: Their resultant is always equal to their sum

questions.explanation: Two vectors cancel only if they are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. With unequal magnitudes, the resultant is at least |A - B| > 0.

questions.question: In the standard representation of a nucleus (A over Z), it indicates:
questions.explanation: Z is the atomic number (protons) and A is the mass number (protons + neutrons), so neutrons = A - Z.

questions.concept: Oxidation number of P in H5P3O10
questions.question: What is the oxidation number of P in H5P3O10?
What is the cause of baldness with increasing age?

options.B: Decreased blood flow to the scalp

questions.explanation: Ageing reduces blood circulation to hair follicles, weakening them and causing hair loss (as per the answer key).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Biodegradable substances persist in the environment for a long time
options.B: Non-biodegradable substances help various components of the ecosystem
options.C: Plastics are broken down quickly by decomposers
options.D: Enzymes, bacteria and other saprophytes act on biodegradable substances and decompose them

questions.explanation: Biodegradable substances are broken down by microbial and enzymatic action. Non-biodegradable substances such as plastics persist and harm the ecosystem.

questions.question: Which of the following increases the heartbeat rapidly in an emergency?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline (the 'fight or flight' hormone) increases heart rate. Acetylcholine (vagus nerve) slows the heart.

questions.question: Using all the letters of the word 'MACHINE', how many words (meaningful or not) can be formed such that the vowels appear only in odd positions?
questions.explanation: 7 letters, 4 odd positions (1,3,5,7). Place 3 vowels (A, I, E) in 4 odd places: 4P3 = 24. Arrange 4 consonants in remaining 4 places: 4! = 24. Total = 24 × 24 = 576.

questions.question: A policeman chases a thief who is 630 m away from him. If they run at 9.5 km/hr and 6.5 km/hr respectively, what distance (in km, to 1 decimal place) does the thief cover before being caught?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 3 km/hr. Time = 0.63/3 = 0.21 hr. Thief's distance = 6.5 × 0.21 = 1.365 ≈ 1.4 km. (2.1 km is the policeman's distance.)

questions.question: In what ratio should a grocer mix two varieties of rice costing ₹128 and ₹143 per kg to obtain a mixture costing ₹137.75 per kg?
A truck driver drove for 3 hours at 60 km/hr, stopped for 1 hour, then drove for 4 more hours at 60 km/hr. What was the average speed (in km/hr)?
questions.explanation: Distance = 180 + 240 = 420 km. Total time including the stop = 8 hr. Average = 420/8 = 52.5 km/hr.

questions.question: If the product of two numbers is 726 and their HCF is 11, what is their LCM?
questions.explanation: HCF × LCM = product, so LCM = 726 / 11 = 66.

questions.question: A certain sum was lent at 10% per annum compound interest (compounded annually) for 1 year 9 months. If the compound interest is ₹1460, find the sum lent.
questions.explanation: For the fractional year, interest is added at the proportional rate: amount factor = 1.10 × (1 + 0.10 × 9/12) = 1.10 × 1.075 = 1.1825. CI = 0.1825P = 1460, so P = ₹8000.

questions.question: Which term of the AP 25, 20, 15, ... is the first negative term?
questions.explanation: a_n = 25 - 5(n - 1) < 0 gives n > 6, so the 7th term (-5) is the first negative term. The 6th term is 0.

questions.question: A number is first increased by 10%, then by 20%, and then decreased by 12%. What is the net percentage change in the original number?
questions.explanation: 1.10 × 1.20 × 0.88 = 1.1616, a net increase of 16.16%. Simply adding (10 + 20 - 12 = 18%) is wrong.

questions.question: 'Parakram Diwas' is celebrated every year on 23 January in India on the birth anniversary of whom?
questions.explanation: Since 2021, 23 January (birth anniversary of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose) is observed as Parakram Diwas.

questions.question: How much investment did Microsoft announce in AI and cloud infrastructure in India over the next two years (January 2025)?
questions.explanation: In January 2025, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced a US$3 billion investment in India's AI and cloud infrastructure.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the new CEO of UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India)?
questions.explanation: IAS officer Bhuvnesh Kumar was appointed CEO of UIDAI in 2025, succeeding Amit Agrawal.

questions.question: What rank has India secured among 145 countries in the Global Firepower Index 2025?
questions.explanation: Global Firepower Index 2025: USA 1st, Russia 2nd, China 3rd, India 4th.

questions.question: Under Project Cheetah, in which wildlife sanctuary/national park will the 8 cheetahs brought from Botswana be relocated?
questions.explanation: The cheetahs from Botswana are to be housed at Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary (Madhya Pradesh), the second site after Kuno National Park.

questions.question: Alka Singh became the first female player from which state to win a gold medal (wrestling) in the Khelo India Youth Games 2025?
questions.explanation: Alka Singh won gold in wrestling at KIYG 2025 (held in Bihar), becoming the first female wrestler from Bihar to do so.

questions.question: Who became the youngest player to score a century in IPL history?
questions.explanation: 14-year-old Vaibhav Suryavanshi (Rajasthan Royals) scored a 35-ball century against Gujarat Titans in IPL 2025.

questions.question: ISRO's PSLV-C61 mission carrying the EOS-09 Earth observation satellite was unsuccessful. It was ISRO's which launch from Sriharikota?
questions.explanation: PSLV-C61 (18 May 2025) was ISRO's 101st launch from Sriharikota; it failed due to a third-stage anomaly. The 100th was GSLV-F15.

questions.question: In process synchronization, which mechanism involves a process continuously checking a condition, thus consuming CPU cycles?
questions.explanation: In busy waiting (spin lock), the process loops on a condition and wastes CPU cycles. Blocking semaphores and monitors put the process to sleep instead.

questions.question: Which scheduling algorithm can potentially lead to starvation of low-priority processes?
questions.explanation: In priority scheduling, high-priority processes can keep low-priority ones waiting indefinitely; aging solves this. FCFS and RR are starvation-free.

questions.question: What does the "ACID" acronym in database transactions stand for?
questions.explanation: ACID = Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.

questions.question: If a relation is in 3NF, it must also be in which normal form?
questions.explanation: Normal forms are cumulative: 3NF implies 2NF and 1NF. A 3NF relation need not be in BCNF or higher.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing packets from source to destination across multiple networks?
questions.explanation: The Network Layer (Layer 3) handles logical addressing (IP) and routing between networks.

questions.question: Which protocol commonly operates over UDP (User Datagram Protocol)?
questions.explanation: DNS queries use UDP port 53. HTTP, FTP and SMTP run over TCP.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity for searching an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (BST)?
questions.explanation: A balanced BST has height O(log n), so search is O(log n). O(n) is the worst case of an unbalanced (skewed) BST.

questions.question: Breadth-First Search (BFS) uses which data structure?
questions.explanation: BFS explores level by level using a FIFO queue. DFS uses a stack.

questions.question: Which type of grammar is recognized by a Pushdown Automaton?
questions.explanation: PDA ↔ context-free (Type-2). Finite automata ↔ regular, LBA ↔ context-sensitive, Turing machine ↔ recursively enumerable.

questions.question: The phase of a compiler that produces an intermediate representation (e.g. three-address code) from the parse tree is known as?
questions.explanation: After semantic analysis checks the annotated parse tree, the intermediate code generator translates it into an IR such as three-address code.

questions.question: What is the memory hierarchy in a computer system, ordered from fastest to slowest?
questions.explanation: Registers (inside the CPU) are fastest, then cache, then main memory (RAM), then secondary storage.

questions.question: Which instruction format typically has no explicit operands?
questions.explanation: 0-address instructions are used in stack machines; operands are implicitly taken from the top of the stack.

questions.question: The mechanism of binding data and the methods that operate on that data into a single unit is known as?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation wraps data and methods into a single unit (class) and hides internal state.

questions.question: What type of inheritance involves a class deriving from more than one base class?
questions.explanation: Multiple inheritance: one derived class, several base classes. Hierarchical is the reverse (several derived from one base).

questions.question: Which software development model is characterized by a sequential design process?
questions.explanation: The Waterfall model proceeds linearly through phases, each completing before the next begins.

questions.question: Which type of testing is performed by the end-user or client to ensure the software meets their requirements?
questions.explanation: Acceptance testing (UAT, alpha/beta) is done by users/clients to validate that the software meets business requirements.

questions.question: What is a "Man-in-the-Middle" (MITM) attack?

options.A: An attacker secretly intercepts and possibly alters communication between two parties
options.B: An attacker guesses passwords by trying all combinations
options.C: An attacker floods a system with heavy traffic
options.D: An attacker pretends to be a trusted entity

questions.explanation: In MITM, the attacker sits between two communicating parties. Flooding is DoS, pretending is spoofing/phishing, and guessing is brute force.

questions.question: Which language is primarily used for styling web pages?
questions.explanation: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls presentation; HTML provides structure and JavaScript provides behaviour.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an unsupervised learning algorithm?
questions.explanation: K-Means groups unlabeled data into clusters. Regression, SVM and decision tree classifiers need labeled data (supervised).

questions.question: What is the core idea behind the "MapReduce" programming model?

options.A: Splitting data into smaller chunks and processing them in parallel
options.B: Processing data only in real time
options.C: Storing data in a single centralized database
options.D: Processing data in a strictly sequential manner

questions.explanation: MapReduce maps input splits to key-value pairs in parallel across nodes and then reduces (aggregates) them.

questions.question: The problem where a set of processes are in a circular wait for resources is known as?
questions.explanation: Circular wait is one of the four Coffman conditions; when all hold, the processes are deadlocked.

questions.question: Which memory allocation policy results in the smallest leftover hole in memory?
questions.explanation: Best-fit chooses the smallest hole that is large enough, leaving the smallest leftover. Worst-fit leaves the largest.

questions.question: Which SQL clause is used to filter results based on an aggregate function?
questions.explanation: HAVING filters groups after aggregation (e.g. HAVING COUNT(*) > 5). WHERE filters rows before grouping and cannot use aggregates.

questions.question: A NoSQL database that stores data in document-like structures (e.g. JSON) is known as?
questions.explanation: Document databases such as MongoDB store JSON/BSON documents.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Transport Layer in the TCP/IP model?
questions.explanation: The transport layer (TCP/UDP) provides end-to-end, process-to-process delivery using port numbers, with error control. Hop-to-hop is the data link layer.

questions.question: Which of the following IP addresses is a private IP address?
A full binary tree with L leaves has how many total nodes?
questions.explanation: In a full binary tree, internal nodes = L - 1, so total = L + (L - 1) = 2L - 1.

questions.question: Which algorithm finds the shortest path in a weighted graph with negative weight edges but no negative cycles?
questions.explanation: Bellman-Ford handles negative edges and detects negative cycles. Dijkstra fails with negative edges; Prim and Kruskal find MSTs.

questions.question: A Finite Automaton can recognize which class of languages?
questions.explanation: Finite automata (DFA/NFA) recognize exactly the regular languages.

questions.question: Removing left recursion from a grammar is a technique required for?
questions.explanation: Top-down (recursive descent, LL) parsers loop infinitely on left recursion, so it must be eliminated. LR parsers handle left recursion.

questions.question: A flip-flop is the basic building block of which type of circuit?
questions.explanation: A flip-flop stores one bit of state, which is the defining feature of sequential circuits (registers, counters).

questions.question: The von Neumann architecture is characterized by?

options.A: Shared memory for data and instructions
options.C: No need for a program counter

questions.explanation: Von Neumann uses a single memory and bus for both programs and data (stored-program concept). Separate memories define the Harvard architecture.

questions.question: Which OOP concept allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method already provided by its superclass?
questions.explanation: Overriding redefines an inherited method with the same signature in the subclass (runtime polymorphism).

questions.question: A special method that is automatically called when an object is created is known as a?
questions.explanation: A constructor initializes an object when it is created; a destructor runs when the object is destroyed.

questions.question: "Black Box Testing" focuses on what aspect of the software?
questions.explanation: Black box testing checks inputs against expected outputs without knowledge of internal code. Internal structure is tested in white box testing.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key activity in the Agile software development methodology?
questions.explanation: Agile (e.g. Scrum) uses short iterations and daily stand-ups; heavy documentation and fixed sequential phases are Waterfall traits.

questions.question: An attack where a malicious actor inserts malicious code into a trusted website, which then gets executed in a victim's browser, is called?
questions.explanation: XSS injects scripts that run in the victim's browser. SQL injection targets the database; CSRF tricks a user into sending unwanted requests.

questions.question: Which JavaScript keyword declares a variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: 'const' creates a binding that cannot be reassigned. 'var' and 'let' allow reassignment.

questions.question: In machine learning, the bias-variance tradeoff involves minimizing two sources of error. What is high variance associated with?
questions.explanation: High variance means the model fits noise in training data and generalizes poorly: overfitting. High bias / simple models cause underfitting.

questions.question: What is a "Generative Adversarial Network" (GAN)?

options.A: A neural network model that clusters data
options.B: A single network trained only to classify images
options.D: A model with two neural networks (a generator and a discriminator) that compete to generate new data

questions.explanation: A GAN pits a generator (creating fake samples) against a discriminator (distinguishing real from fake).

questions.question: In virtual memory systems, the situation where a process spends more time paging than executing is called?
questions.explanation: Thrashing is excessive paging due to insufficient frames, causing CPU utilization to collapse.

questions.question: What is an inode in a Unix-like file system?

options.C: A data structure that stores metadata about a file
options.D: The actual data block of the file

questions.explanation: An inode stores file metadata (size, owner, permissions, timestamps, block pointers) but not the file name or data.

questions.question: Which SQL statement is used to remove a table from a database?
questions.explanation: DROP TABLE deletes the table structure and data. TRUNCATE removes only the rows; DELETE TABLE and REMOVE TABLE are not valid.

questions.question: Which normal form deals with transitive dependencies?
questions.explanation: 3NF removes transitive dependencies of non-key attributes on the key. 2NF removes partial dependencies; 4NF removes multivalued dependencies.

questions.question: The physical layer of the OSI model is concerned with the transmission of what over a physical medium?
questions.explanation: PDUs: physical layer = bits, data link = frames, network = packets, transport = segments.

questions.question: What is the purpose of NAT (Network Address Translation)?

options.A: To determine routing paths in a network
options.B: To map private IP addresses to public IP addresses and vice versa
options.C: To assign IP addresses dynamically to hosts

questions.explanation: NAT translates private addresses to public ones at the router. Encryption is done by IPsec/TLS; dynamic assignment is DHCP.

questions.question: What does it mean for an algorithm to be "in-place"?

options.A: It preserves the relative order of equal elements
options.B: It uses only a constant amount of extra memory relative to the input size
options.C: It always finds the optimal solution
options.D: It always runs in O(n log n) time

questions.explanation: In-place algorithms need O(1) (or very small) auxiliary space. Preserving order of equal elements is 'stable'.

questions.question: A dynamic programming approach solves problems by?

options.A: Breaking them into overlapping sub-problems and storing their solutions
options.B: Making a locally optimal choice at each step
options.D: Dividing the problem into independent sub-problems

questions.explanation: DP uses overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure with memoization/tabulation. Local choice is greedy; independent subproblems is divide and conquer.

questions.question: What is a "Regular Expression"?

options.A: A sequence of characters that describes a search pattern in text
options.D: A data structure for storing strings

questions.explanation: A regular expression is a pattern notation that describes a regular language and is used for searching and matching text.

questions.question: LR parsers are an example of which type of parsing?
questions.explanation: LR parsers (SLR, LALR, CLR) use shift-reduce, which is bottom-up. Recursive descent and LL(1) are top-down.

questions.question: A multiplexer (MUX) is a digital circuit that does what?

options.A: Directs one input to one of several output lines
options.B: Selects one of several input lines and forwards it to a single output line
options.D: Stores a single bit of data

questions.explanation: A MUX is a data selector (many to one). Routing one input to many outputs is a demultiplexer.

questions.question: In computer architecture, what is "Amdahl's Law" used for?

options.A: To measure the clock speed of a CPU
options.C: To predict the theoretical maximum speedup after improving a part of the system
options.D: To determine the cache hit rate

questions.explanation: Amdahl's Law: Speedup = 1 / ((1 - f) + f/s), where f is the fraction improved by factor s.

questions.question: A C++ function declared with the friend keyword can access which members of a class?
questions.explanation: A friend function is granted access to all members of the class, including private and protected ones.

questions.question: The 'this' pointer (or reference) in C++ or Java refers to what?

options.A: A static member of the class
options.C: The class itself, not an object
options.D: The current object on which the method is invoked

questions.explanation: 'this' refers to the invoking object. 'super' (Java) refers to the parent part; static members have no 'this'.

questions.question: "Coupling" in software design refers to the degree of...?

options.B: Relatedness of elements within a single module

questions.explanation: Coupling is dependency between modules (aim: low). Relatedness within a module is cohesion (aim: high).

questions.question: The practice of breaking code changes into small, frequent updates that are integrated and tested automatically is known as?
questions.explanation: CI/CD merges small changes frequently and runs automated builds and tests on each change.

questions.question: A "digital signature" provides which of the following sets of security services?
questions.explanation: A digital signature (hash signed with the sender's private key) proves who sent the message, that it was not altered, and prevents denial. It does not provide confidentiality.

questions.question: What does REST stand for in the context of web APIs?
questions.explanation: REST = Representational State Transfer, an architectural style defined by Roy Fielding.

questions.question: Which type of Artificial Neural Network is specifically designed to process sequential data like time series or natural language?
questions.explanation: RNNs have recurrent connections (memory) to handle sequences. CNNs are mainly for grid data such as images.

questions.question: The process of extracting useful features from raw data to facilitate machine learning tasks is called?
questions.explanation: Feature engineering creates and selects informative input variables from raw data.

questions.question: In cloud computing, what does "IaaS" stand for?
questions.explanation: IaaS provides virtualized computing resources (VMs, storage, networks), e.g. AWS EC2.

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of a blockchain?

options.A: Its records can be freely edited by any user
options.B: It is used only for financial transactions
options.C: It is an immutable, distributed ledger
options.D: It is centralized and stored on a single server

questions.explanation: Blockchain is a decentralized, tamper-resistant ledger where blocks are chained by cryptographic hashes.

questions.question: Which technology is a core component of the Internet of Things (IoT), allowing devices to communicate with each other?
questions.explanation: IoT relies on sensors and wireless communication; WSNs collect and transmit data between devices.

questions.question: What is the "halting problem" in computability theory?

options.A: The problem of calculating the memory required by a program
options.B: The problem of finding the fastest algorithm for a task
options.C: The problem of deciding whether two programs are equivalent
options.D: The problem of deciding whether a given program will halt or run forever on a given input

questions.explanation: Turing proved the halting problem is undecidable: no algorithm can decide halting for every program-input pair.

questions.question: Which attack involves overwhelming a server or network with traffic to make it unavailable to its intended users?
questions.explanation: A DDoS attack floods the target from many compromised machines, exhausting its resources.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a cookie in web browsing?

options.A: To let a web server remember stateful information about the user's browsing activity
options.B: To encrypt data sent to the server

questions.explanation: HTTP is stateless; cookies store small data (session IDs, preferences) in the browser so the server can recognise the user.

questions.question: The hexadecimal representation of the decimal number 26 is?
Which logic gate is known as a universal gate?
questions.explanation: NAND and NOR are universal gates; any Boolean function can be built using only them.

questions.question: In a graph, a path that visits each vertex exactly once is called a?
questions.explanation: A Hamiltonian path visits every vertex once. An Eulerian path traverses every edge exactly once.

questions.question: Which data structure is most suitable for implementing a priority queue?
questions.explanation: A binary heap gives O(log n) insert and delete-max/min and O(1) access to the top priority element.

questions.question: Shortest Job First (SJF) is an optimal scheduling algorithm in terms of?
questions.explanation: SJF is provably optimal for minimum average waiting time for a given set of processes, but can starve long jobs.

questions.question: What does a "Foreign Key" in a relational database enforce?
questions.explanation: A foreign key must match a primary key value in the referenced table (or be NULL), enforcing referential integrity. Entity integrity is enforced by the primary key.

questions.question: Which protocol provides a secure channel over an insecure network in a client-server architecture?
questions.explanation: SSH (port 22) encrypts remote login and commands. Telnet and FTP send data, including passwords, in plain text.

questions.question: Which software testing level focuses on testing individual components or modules?
questions.explanation: Unit testing checks the smallest testable parts in isolation, usually by developers.

questions.question: In object-oriented programming, a class that cannot be instantiated is called?
questions.explanation: An abstract class (often with abstract/pure virtual methods) cannot be instantiated. A final class cannot be inherited.

questions.question: In image processing, the technique of partitioning a digital image into multiple segments (sets of pixels) is known as?
questions.explanation: Segmentation divides an image into meaningful regions; enhancement improves appearance and restoration removes degradation.

questions.question: What is the primary function of an operating system's kernel?

options.D: Managing communication between hardware and software

questions.explanation: The kernel is the core of the OS that manages CPU, memory and devices and mediates between hardware and software. The shell/GUI provides the interface.

questions.question: The time taken by a disk drive to position the read/write head over the desired track is known as?
questions.explanation: Seek time moves the head to the track; rotational latency waits for the sector to come under the head. Access time = seek + latency.

questions.question: The total number of subtrees (one rooted at each node) in a complete binary tree of depth d (root at depth 0) is?
questions.explanation: A complete binary tree of depth d has 2^(d+1) - 1 nodes, and each node is the root of exactly one subtree.

questions.question: A server that sits between a client application and a real server, intercepting all requests, is known as a?
questions.explanation: A proxy server acts as an intermediary: it receives client requests, forwards them, and can cache or filter them.
